blindSummary:
A gender-inclusive-language ban has been in force in this state/province's entire public administration, schools and universities since 1 April 2024, following a government declaration by the state/province's premier and a cabinet decision. A visitor dealing with any registry office, police station, hospital admission desk or school operates in an environment where official gender-inclusive framing is prohibited — dismissed by critics as "pure symbol politics", but practically a standing instruction of institutional coldness at every public counter. The state/province is also a partner in an initiative, tabled by several of its neighbours in the federal upper house, to tighten the federal law on legal gender self-identification.

The state/province's police recorded 2,021 hate crimes in 2024 (up 8.2 % from 1,867 in 2023), but the LGBTQ+-specific breakdown was contested in a parliamentary query, and the framework dossier cautions that the comparatively high counts may reflect better police classification rather than greater danger. No documented street-violence incident specific to a trans visitor was found here in this pass. The record shows institutional posture rather than demonstrated violence: the language ban applies at every public counter, and no comparable physical-attack evidence or equality-dismantling bill is part of this state/province's own file.
blindSourceSummaries: A public broadcaster's report on this state/province's gender-language ban: from 1 April 2024, gender-inclusive forms of the national language are prohibited in schools, universities and all state administration, implementing the government declaration of December 2023 and a cabinet decision amending the language rules of public authorities; critics in the coverage dismiss it as symbol politics while noting its practical reach across every public counter, registry office and classroom.

A regional radio report on the federal upper-house initiative by several states/provinces — this state/province a partner — to tighten the federal law on legal gender self-identification, i.e. an organised state-level attempt to make the nationwide self-ID law stricter.

The state/province's interior ministry press release (from its interior minister) presenting the 2024 hate-crime situation report: 2,021 recorded hate-crime offences, up 8.2 % on 2023's 1,867, published as the state's own situation survey; the framework dossier notes the LGBTQ+ sub-category was contested in a parliamentary query and that the comparatively high counts may reflect more thorough police classification rather than greater danger.
